data.name: Rig n Roll
data.detailed_description:
Players will step into the shoes of a young man in the year 2014 as he arrives in California to pursue his dreams of road domination and capture the Californian cargo transportation market. There are miles of highways to conquer and cities and towns to reach as he becomes the greatest trucker on the highways. Rig’n’Roll is a sequel to the famous Hard Truck series. This time the game world is true-to-life. Gamers can race high-powered Semis along thousands miles of real Californian roads, visiting San-Francisco to San Diego, San Jose to Los Angeles. Rig’n’Roll delivers players the ultimate truck driving experience with authentic models of trucks and their interiors, completely new physics and astonishing 3D graphics among numerous features.
Players will outrun their opponents to deliver cargo on time or take part in truck races to prove their professional skills, giving them the opportunity to improve their rating and authority among other drivers. Rig’n’Roll also gives gamers an opportunity to test their management skills as they establish their own cargo transportation company. Players will recruit staff and hire other drivers to work for them as they expand their business and eliminate their competitors from the transportation market. Apart from being the most accurate and innovative truck driving simulation game ever produced, Rig’n’Roll immerses players in an exciting story with an unexpected finale, making new allies and battling treacherous foes as they discover a conspiracy that will test their skills to the limit.
Key features:
  • Authentic models of famous trucks — Freightliner, Peterbilt, Kenworth, Sterling and Western Star
  • Over 12,000 miles of California roads, including all major freeways
  • Over 40 California cities, including San Diego, San Francisco and Los Angeles
  • Truck races, cargo delivery, economic simulation and a thrilling storyline

reviews.review:
Rig 'n' Roll is an ambitious trucking simulation developed by SoftLab-NSK and published by Fulqrum Publishing that sets itself apart by blending realistic long-haul driving with business management, competitive truck racing, and a narrative-driven campaign. Rather than limiting players to a straightforward cargo delivery experience, the game creates a broader journey in which every successful delivery contributes to building both a personal reputation and a growing transportation empire. Although its technology reflects its era, its willingness to combine several gameplay styles results in an experience that remains distinctive within the truck simulation genre.

The story follows an aspiring truck driver who arrives in California determined to become one of the state's most respected freight operators. As the career progresses, routine delivery contracts gradually evolve into a larger adventure involving rival companies, unexpected allies, and a conspiracy that gives the campaign more purpose than simply earning money. This narrative structure adds motivation to each job and provides a sense of progression that is often absent from more traditional driving simulators. Players are constantly working toward expanding their influence while uncovering new events that keep the campaign engaging from beginning to end.

The recreation of California is one of the game's strongest achievements. Featuring over 12,000 miles of roads and more than forty cities, the map captures the scale of interstate trucking with highways stretching between recognizable locations such as San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, and San Jose. Long-distance trips create an authentic feeling of life behind the wheel, while changing scenery helps reduce repetition during lengthy deliveries. Even if the graphics no longer match modern standards, the world still succeeds in conveying the atmosphere of commercial trucking across a large and varied landscape.

Driving mechanics successfully balance accessibility with realism. A selection of licensed trucks from respected manufacturers, complete with detailed interiors, gives each vehicle a satisfying sense of authenticity. Vehicle handling emphasizes weight, momentum, and careful maneuvering without becoming overly punishing for newcomers. Traffic regulations also play an important role, encouraging responsible driving through police enforcement and financial penalties for reckless behavior. This creates an experience where safe and efficient driving becomes just as rewarding as speed.

Beyond standard deliveries, Rig 'n' Roll introduces truck racing events that inject energy into the campaign. These competitions challenge players to master vehicle handling while competing directly against rival drivers for reputation and rewards. Combined with timed cargo deliveries, these events prevent the gameplay from becoming repetitive and reinforce the game's identity as something more adventurous than a conventional trucking simulator.

Management mechanics further expand the experience by allowing players to establish and operate their own freight company. Earnings can be invested into purchasing additional trucks, recruiting drivers, assigning contracts, and steadily expanding the business throughout California. Watching a small operation develop into a successful transportation enterprise provides satisfying long-term progression and gives financial decisions genuine importance. Balancing company growth with personal driving responsibilities creates an enjoyable strategic layer that complements the simulation mechanics.

Visually, the game still offers respectable truck models, convincing weather effects, and atmospheric highways despite its age. The environments effectively communicate the scale of the open world, while engine sounds and environmental audio reinforce the sensation of spending long hours on the road. Cinematic sequences and voice acting help support the story, although some animations and presentation elements clearly reveal the game's original release period. Technical limitations, occasional interface frustrations, and inconsistent artificial intelligence can sometimes interrupt immersion, but they rarely overshadow the overall experience.

Rig 'n' Roll remains memorable because it refuses to focus solely on cargo transportation. It successfully combines open-world exploration, truck simulation, company management, racing events, and an engaging storyline into a package that still feels refreshingly different from many other trucking games. While players seeking the polish and realism of newer simulators may notice its aging mechanics, those willing to embrace its unique design will discover a surprisingly deep and rewarding experience with plenty of variety.

Rating: 6/10
